# JPEG orientation fixtures

Project-authored quadrants and circle under the repository MIT license. generate.py uses Pillow 12.3.0 to generate eight JPEG EXIF orientations and independent, decoded/oriented PNG references. Tests use the checked-in files; Python is optional fixture tooling. The two-channel-value comparison tolerance accounts for JPEG decoder differences, not geometric drift. Browser checks separately report edge/scaling differences and reject a deliberately incorrect orientation.

Browser acceptance checks all eight native-resolution decodes against their Pillow references with the same two-channel-value limit. For the enlarged SVG, it uses the original Pillow PNG and eight explicit EXIF matrices, preserving the JPEG decoder's original pixel coordinate system during interpolation. The aggregate limits remain mean channel error ≤ 1 and at most 2% of channels differing by more than 10. Every fit/crop case must reject both a wrong orientation and a swapped fit/crop mode. The earlier comparison with pre-oriented PNGs remains in each report as a sampling diagnostic; macOS Chromium 153 differed at enlarged mirrored edges despite identical native-resolution pixels. See the [release investigation](../../../docs/evidence/release-0.8.0/README.md).
